three.text: The third model is built on three metabolic engines that power all human action. Here is the power you can produce, against the duration of the effort. Each engine dominates a different range of power and duration.

phosphagen.text: First, the phosphagen engine. It runs on stored ATP and creatine phosphate, and it rebuilds ATP without oxygen. Immediate, explosive power, but the store is tiny, and it is largely spent within 10 to 15 seconds of all-out effort.

glycolytic.text: Next, the glycolytic engine, running on muscle glycogen and blood glucose. It breaks down carbohydrate without oxygen, to lactate. It takes over as the phosphagens fall, and it peaks near 15 to 30 seconds. Its capacity is capped by the acid it accumulates.

oxidative.text: Then the oxidative engine: carbohydrate and fat, burned with oxygen. Slow to ramp, but enormous in capacity. It overtakes the anaerobic systems past about 75 seconds, and within the hour it supplies more than 90 percent of the energy.

power.source: caption (Height is power output; Oxidative outlasts the others, it is not more powerful); PEAK_ORDER_TEXT
power.text: Now pull the three apart. Height is power output. The phosphagen engine peaks highest, then the glycolytic, then the oxidative. So the oxidative engine is not more powerful. It simply outlasts the others.

workouts.source: ENERGY_BENCHMARKS (1RM Lift 3 s, 400m 50 s, Fran 240 s, 5k Run 1320 s, and their dominant engines); caption
workouts.text: Now put real efforts on the curve, and watch the dominant engine change. A one-rep max lift, about 3 seconds: phosphagen. A 400 meter run: glycolytic. Fran, about 4 minutes: oxidative. And a 5k run, oxidative again.

all-three.source: MODULE_COPY pathways s3 to s4; keyPoints (under about 10 seconds; up to a couple of minutes; beyond); ENERGY_SYSTEMS durations
all-three.text: Total fitness requires training all three engines: the short bursts under about 10 seconds, the efforts up to about two minutes, and everything beyond. The two most common faults in fitness training are favoring one or two, and over-training the oxidative engine.
